methods.label: Eliminate a shared expression
methods.explanation:
The term \(x/y\) requires \(y\ne0\). From the first two terms, the common difference is
\[
d=(x-y)-(x+y)=-2y.
\]
Continuing with this difference, the third and fourth terms must be \(x-3y\) and \(x-5y\). Therefore
\[
xy=x-3y,
\qquad
\frac{x}{y}=x-5y.
\]
We can rearrange both equations to contain the same expression, \(x(y-1)\), so that comparing them eliminates \(x\). The first gives
\[
x(y-1)=-3y.
\]
Multiplying the second by the nonzero number \(y\) gives \(x=xy-5y^2\), or
\[
x(y-1)=5y^2.
\]
Consequently, \(5y^2=-3y\). Since \(y\ne0\), division by \(y\) gives \(5y=-3\), so \(y=-3/5\). Substituting into the first identity gives
\[
x\left(-\frac85\right)=\frac95,
\qquad x=-\frac98.
\]
These values give the original four terms
\[
-\frac{69}{40},\quad-\frac{21}{40},\quad
\frac{27}{40},\quad\frac{75}{40},
\]
whose consecutive differences are all \(48/40\). They satisfy the original conditions, and the nonzero condition on \(y\) has excluded the only canceled possibility. The fifth term is
\[
\frac{75}{40}+\frac{48}{40}
=\boxed{\frac{123}{40}},
\]
choice \(\text{E}\).
